Hi Evelyn — great timing. Thanks for the specifics.

High-level options (budgetary figures; will follow with a pro forma PDF + split schedule):
1) Annual upfront (12 months) — Standard list rate with 5% prepaid discount. Option to invoice upfront or split across 4 quarterly invoices; if split, discount applies upon first invoice and credit memo applied across the remaining invoices.
2) 2-year prepaid commit — 8% term discount, can be invoiced as 100% upfront or 50/50 by year; we can also structure as an annual invoice with a 50% deposit + balance if you need Opex alignment.
3) 3-year prepaid commit — 10% term discount + price protection clause for model catalog parity; suggested escrow release schedule tied to quarterly uptime & consumption milestones.

Escrow/Refunds: we typically accept an escrow vehicle for a portion of the deposit (suggested 20% of upfront) held by a neutral custodian and released quarterly based on SLA/uptake milestones. Alternatively, we can provide a refundable credit with clearly defined clawback triggers (SLA breach window or sustained under-consumption).

Ramp commitments: if you expect a significant ramp (e.g., 3x usage over 6 months), we can price in staged throughput thresholds so you don't overcommit on peak capacity.

I'll prepare a concise pro forma and a split-invoicing schedule and loop in finance/legal internally to confirm the escrow language. Expect those documents by Monday (6/1).

Best,

Team — reviewed with finance and legal. Suggested changes:
1) Discounts: keep 5/8/10% bands but show an alternate 2-year 9% mid-band if Brightline agrees to a 12-month minimum spend floor in year one. We can use the mid-band as a negotiation lever.
2) Escrow: propose 12% custodied holdback for 2-yr, 15% for 3-yr. Redwood will absorb custodian setup fee up to $3k, not ongoing annual fees. If custodian insists on ongoing fees >$5k/year, we pass that through.
3) Refund mechanics: operationalize as a refundable credit applied to future invoices with a 180-day review point (i.e., if consumption < threshold after 180 days, a pro-rated credit is returned). Legal prefers credits vs cash refunds to limit cash flow churn.
4) Split invoicing: we can do split across 4 quarterly invoices for the upfront element. When split is used, the full discount is recognized on the invoice schedule and we issue an offsetting credit memo if refund/credit triggers later.

I've attached a draft pro forma and an XLS that shows FY27 cash outlay vs PAYG and net ARR impact. Also attached a short escrow term sheet for their counsel to review.
